top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) are a new measurement capability built on the magic-wavelength concept, realised and reproduced across independent laboratories with agreeing clock comparisons at the 1e-18 level. The two-name allocation is compact and the citation can be written around the physics (many-atom interrogation with the light shift cancelled) rather than the application or the redefinition of the second. P002 is a credible second choice (prediction followed by surprising, widely reproduced experiment) but I am outside my competence on it, the pairing mechanism is still debated and the credit question around Yuan Cao is unresolved. A year without an award is worse than either, since a mature, well-documented achievement is available.
recusal_note: Direct field overlap with circuit QED (not on the slate); I direct WACQT and am a Chalmers MC2 colleague of Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson. No connection to the laureates in P001 or P002 apparent from profile, so no recusal needed for this slate.
